title: Freight HSN Code and GST Rate: A Guide to Freight Charges
summary: Check freight charges HSN code 9965, GST rates, GTA reverse charge, ITC conditions and when delivery charges follow the HSN code and GST rate of goods.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


### Key Takeaways


- Freight charges generally fall under SAC 9965, the heading for goods transport services. “Freight HSN code” is the common search term.
- There is no single freight GST rate. Taxable GTA services commonly attract 5% or 18%, while specified transport services are exempt.
- Delivery naturally bundled with goods can follow the goods’ classification and GST rate, even when freight is listed separately.
- Check the consignment note, charge mechanism and ITC conditions before accepting or issuing a freight invoice.


##


Freight HSN Code Explained


The code commonly searched as the freight HSN code is **SAC 9965** . This heading applies to goods transport services, including road, rail, water, air and pipeline transport. Freight is a service, so SAC is the technically correct term.


If your company supplies an independent freight service, you typically would use SAC 9965 or a relevant sub-code. A separate invoice line alone does not establish a separate supply. However, when the freight costs are charged together with the cost of goods purchased, the application of the HSN code and[GST rates](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/new-gst-rates/) for the goods being purchased may take precedence over using SAC 9965. The choice of which SAC code to use can have implications regarding the accuracy of the invoice, eligibility for[input tax credit (ITC)](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/input-tax-credit-gst/) ,[e-way bill requirements](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/eway-bill-online-generation/) and GST returns. Therefore, this guide outlines when to use SAC 9965, when to use the HSN code of the goods being delivered and the applicability of GST to freight costs in India.


##


What Is the HSN Code for Freight Charges?


In general, the code for freight costs is SAC 9965. SAC refers to Services Accounting Code and HSN refers to Harmonized System of Nomenclature, which is utilized for goods. In practice, searches often use “freight charges HSN code”, but[HSN and SAC codes](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/hsn-sac-code-gst/) classify different types of supply.


SAC 9965 represents “goods transport services”. Therefore, it encompasses all modes of transport (i.e., land/sea/air/pipeline) and also represents services provided by a Goods Transport Agency (“GTA”).


Therefore, if a transporter issues an invoice only for transporting goods from one location to another, SAC 9965 is generally the applicable HSN/SAC code. In addition, there are several sub-codes of SAC 9965 that depend upon how the goods were transported.


##


Freight Charges HSN Code and GST Rate in India


There is no uniform GST rate for each freight invoice. Instead, the GST rate depends on various factors, namely:


- Mode of transport;
- Type of service provider; and
- Whether freight is an independent service or part of a composite supply of goods.


For taxable standalone freight, GST rates commonly include **5% or 18%** . Exemptions also apply: ordinary road transport other than GTA or courier services, and goods transport by inland waterways, are generally exempt. Specially notified delivery services have separate conditions.


For taxable GTA services, the GST rate is typically 5% or 18%, depending on the applicable option. The[Ministry of Finance’s GST reform FAQs](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2163560&lang=2&reg=48) explain the 5% rate without the GTA’s input credit and the 18% forward-charge option with ITC.


Service HSN/SAC code Treatment under GST laws


Goods road transport via GTA 9965 / relevant sub-code Generally 5% or 18%, subject to the GTA’s option, exemptions and charge mechanism


Railway goods transport 9965 / relevant sub-code Rate depends upon the service entry and conditions


Water goods transport 9965 / relevant sub-code Rate depends upon the service entry; inland waterway freight is generally exempt


Air goods transport 9965 / relevant sub-code Rate depends upon the service entry and applicable exemptions


Courier services 9968 Generally 18%; separately notified delivery services need their own assessment


Freight bundled with goods as a composite supply HSN code of the principal supply GST rate of the principal supply, usually the goods


Prior to issuing an invoice, please refer to the most recent Central Board of Indirect Taxes & Customs (“CBIC”) notification and the current GST rate schedule. These classifications and conditions can change.


***Also Read:[New GST Rates and Updated GST Slabs in India](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/new-gst-rates/)***


##


Standalone Freight vs Freight Charges Included with Goods


This is where most businesses experience confusion. The arrangement matters more than whether freight is shown on a separate line.


### When Freight Charges Are for a Separate Service


A logistics company that only provides transportation services generally uses SAC 9965 or the relevant sub-code. For example, if a transporter moves a shipment from Pune to Hyderabad and charges only for the transportation cost alone then that service would have been classified under SAC 9965.


The invoice must clearly show the amount of freight costs, applicable GST rate and whether forward charge or reverse charge applies. Confirm any exemption before calculating tax.


### When Freight Charges Form Part of a Goods Supply


Consider a furniture seller. The seller sells furniture worth ₹1,00,000 and adds ₹5,000 for delivery. The customer receives one invoice covering both the furniture and freight costs.


Although the invoice shows furniture and delivery separately, they may form a composite supply if naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business. Where the furniture is the principal supply, its classification and GST rate apply to the combined value. The separate delivery amount does not by itself change this treatment.


The same logic applies to cement, machinery, electronics and other types of goods supplied with delivery. If the supplier is selling goods together with delivery, it should not automatically classify the freight costs under SAC 9965, even when delivery is separately itemized. Review the contract and the substance of the arrangement.


The deciding factor regarding how to report this transaction to GST authorities is what type of arrangement exists between the parties. If the customer purchased goods and freight costs were simply part of fulfilling that purchase order then goods classification generally takes precedence over using SAC 9965. If freight costs represent a distinct service then SAC 9965 may apply.[CBIC’s sectoral FAQs](https://cbic-gst.gov.in/hindi/sectoral-faq.html) illustrate this distinction using delivered-price and ex-works mineral sales.


##


Freight SAC Codes for Road, Rail, Water and Air Transport


SAC 9965 has sub-codes that distinguish between modes of transport. The official service classification annexure provides the structure; confirm the detailed code against the current GST portal master.


SAC code or group Service


9965 Goods transport services


996511 Road transport services of goods; confirm the applicable GTA entry


996512 Rail transport services of goods; verify any specific operator category


996513 Pipeline transport services; verify the commodity-specific description


99652 Water transport services of goods, with detailed codes within this group


996531 Air transport services of letters, parcels and other goods


996519 Other land transport services of goods not elsewhere classified


##


GST on GTA Services: Forward Charge, Reverse Charge and ITC


A Goods Transport Agency (GTA) offers road-based transportation services for goods and issues a consignment note, whatever it is called. Not every truck owner or road transporter is a GTA. GST charged on GTA services will be paid either by the transporter or the recipient depending upon the scenario.


When GTA charges GST on an invoice, it pays the GST to the government. When the recipient pays GST on the freight value based on a notification and applicable conditions, it is called reverse charge.


Generally taxable GTA services attract 5% or 18%. At 5%, the GTA cannot claim input credit on goods and services used to supply that service. At 18% under forward charge, the GTA can claim eligible ITC. These conditions concern the GTA’s own inputs; the customer’s ITC eligibility must be assessed separately. Under reverse charge, the notified recipient generally pays 5% GST, where applicable, and may claim eligible ITC subject to the usual conditions.


Before you accept a freight invoice from a transporter, request that the transporter provide you with information about:


- Whether it issues a consignment note and qualifies as a GTA.
- Is GST payable by the GTA under forward charge or by the recipient under reverse charge?
- Which GST rate and option apply?
- Are there restrictions to claiming input tax credit on the freight?


Confirming these details prior to invoicing can save a great deal of time down the line during reconciliation. Check the transporter’s registration details through[GSTIN verification](https://www.cashfree.com/gst-verification/) as part of vendor onboarding.


##


Example: Separate Freight Invoice at 5% GST


A logistics company transports goods from Pune to Hyderabad and includes freight billed at ₹25,000. Although the logistics company did not sell the goods, it simply provided transport. Assume the GTA has validly opted for 5% forward charge, the registered GTA and recipient are both in Maharashtra, and the place of supply is Maharashtra. The invoice could appear as follows:


Invoice component Amount


Freight value ₹25,000


[CGST](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-cgst-central-goods-and-services-tax/) at 2.5% ₹625


SGST at 2.5% ₹625


Total GST ₹1,250


Invoice total **₹26,250**


This example illustrates how this works, but the actual GST rate and method of payment will vary based upon the classification of the transporter’s business, the transporter’s selection of a GST option and the applicable notification. Cross-check the figures with the[GST calculator](https://www.cashfree.com/gst-calculator/) . The goods’ interstate route alone does not determine the service’s place of supply; apply the relevant[IGST rules](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-igst/) . Under reverse charge, the GTA does not collect this tax from the recipient as part of its invoice total.


##


Example: Freight Charges Included in a Cement Sale


Next consider a cement supplier selling cement valued at ₹90,000 and charging delivery costs of ₹10,000. If the freight costs are naturally included in the sales price of the cement, then the cement supplier may treat the entire invoice value of ₹1,00,000 as one composite supply of cement. In this instance, the cement HSN code and the cement GST rate would apply to all of the invoice value.


At 18%, GST on this illustrative composite supply is ₹18,000, bringing the invoice total to ₹1,18,000.


The cement supplier must not attempt to break out the invoice into two different portions solely to allow it to claim a lower GST rate on the freight portion than it claims on the cement. The proper procedure to follow depends upon your contract with your customer, the type of supply you made to them and any applicable GST provisions.


##


Freight Invoice Requirements and GST Compliance


Just as freight invoices are required to be as legible as goods invoices, they too require clarity. For standalone freight invoices include:


- SAC 9965 or relevant sub-code;
- Service description;
- Origin and destination of consignment;
- Freight value and appropriate GST rate;
- Indication of whether GST is payable under forward charge or reverse charge;
- Consignment note or lorry receipt and supporting delivery proof. A[goods received note](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/goods-received-note-grn/) can support the buyer’s receipt records.


For GTA invoices, also record the consignment’s gross weight, consignor and consignee details, goods carriage registration and GSTIN of the person liable to pay tax.


For freight charges forming part of a composite supply of goods, use the correct HSN code and GST rate of the principal supply. You must ensure that the freight charges are clearly identifiable in the invoice to enable the customer to determine what each component of the invoice represents and how much they owe.


It is also essential to reconcile freight invoices with e-way bills, delivery documents, purchase records and GST returns. Reconciliation will become even more critical if freight charges are regularly incurred by your business and/or if you plan to utilize input tax credits for such charges.


***Also Read:[State-Wise E-Way Bill Limits in India](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/state-wise-eway-bill-limit/)***


##


Common Mistakes with Freight HSN Codes and GST Rates


There are several common errors found in handling freight GST treatment.


- Applying SAC 9965 to delivery charges that form part of a composite supply of goods.
- Charging 18% GST without checking the applicable rate, option or exemption.
- Treating all transporters as GTAs without checking their consignment notes and service arrangements.
- Missing reverse charge requirements for eligible GTA services.
- Confusing the GTA’s own ITC restrictions with the recipient’s eligibility to claim ITC.
- Failing to retain consignment notes, lorry receipts and delivery documents.
- Utilizing vague descriptions such as “Transportation Charges” without accompanying documentation.


A simple rule of thumb for determining if freight charges represent a separate service or are part of a composite supply of goods is to examine your commercial arrangement prior to selecting an HSN code and GST rate.


***Also Read:[Bank Reconciliation: Meaning, Statement and How It Works](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/bank-reconciliation-meaning-statement-and-how-it-works/)***


##


Choosing the Correct HSN Code for Freight Charges


The code commonly called the freight HSN code is SAC 9965 for independent transportation services of goods. However, freight charged together with goods may constitute a single composite supply whereupon both the HSN code and GST rate of the goods shall apply.


As a business, it is necessary to review your commercial arrangement. If freight constitutes a separate transportation service, use SAC 9965 and apply the appropriate GST treatment for transportation services. If freight is naturally combined with other goods supplies, apply HSN codes and GST rates for said goods supplies. Clearly prepared invoices along with proper documentation and correctly classified GST will assist in eliminating potential disputes over input tax credits and potential non-compliance penalties with respect to GST.


For logistics businesses collecting freight payments,[Payment Links](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-links/) can help customers pay against an invoice without a website. The[payment link setup guide](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/no-code/payment-link) explains the workflow. Keep the payment reference linked to the freight invoice and delivery records.


##


FAQs


#### What is the freight HSN code?


The code commonly called the freight HSN code is SAC 9965. It covers goods transport services, including transport by road, rail, water, air and pipeline.


#### What is the freight charges HSN code and GST rate?


For standalone freight charges, businesses generally use SAC 9965. The GST rate may be 5% or 18%, depending on the service type and conditions, while some transport services are exempt. GTA services are commonly taxed at 5% or 18%, depending on the applicable option.


#### Is freight GST always 18%?


No. Freight GST is not always 18%. The rate depends on the mode of transport, the service provider, exemptions and whether freight is an independent service or part of a composite supply.


#### What HSN code should be used when freight is charged with goods?


If freight is part of a composite supply with goods, the HSN code and GST rate of the principal supply, usually the goods, may apply. Businesses should assess the contract terms and applicable GST provisions.


#### What is the SAC code for GTA services?


Goods Transport Agency services generally fall under SAC 9965. The applicable GST rate and tax-payment mechanism depend on the GTA’s option and the recipient’s liability under reverse charge.


#### Can businesses claim input tax credit on freight?


Input tax credit on freight depends on the GST rate option, the nature of the service, and whether GST was paid under forward charge or reverse charge. Businesses should verify eligibility before claiming ITC.
